boundary_decision.rationale: Both independent providers classify provenance as reusable context attached to a host subject or assertion record. The host object, identifier scheme, place, access policy, credential and storage representation remain separate models or referenced services.

decisions.concept: Provenance is a reusable mixin, not the host object
decisions.rationale: Both providers preserve the identity and lifecycle of the host subject while attaching provenance assertions and relationships.

The semantics are accepted, but separate generic class-definition findings are not duplicated because the base structure already covers entity anchoring, activities, agents, attribution and derivation at their governed boundaries.
The base Subject granularity and fixed aspects finding asks the same identity questions while keeping them tied to the provenance subject anchor.

decisions.concept: Generation, usage, communication, start, end and invalidation
decisions.rationale: These event types and their validity constraints sharpen the base relation and activity coverage without changing the boundary.
The base Primary sources and ingredients plus Activity and process step findings already cover resolved dependencies, digests, parameters, inputs, outputs and reproducibility.

decisions.concept: Claim generator, signer and builder trust
decisions.rationale: The distinction is material for C2PA, in-toto and SLSA evidence and complements the generic signed-attestation envelope.
The base Provenance discovery and access finding already covers subject-based discovery, traversal, pingback, downstream notification and availability.

decisions.concept: Structural validity means truth or trust
decisions.rationale: Both passes distinguish syntax and PROV constraints from integrity verification, signer trust, confidence and the truth of the represented claim.

decisions.concept: Legal title, physical custody, attribution and responsibility are interchangeable
decisions.rationale: They are separate relations with different authorities, evidence and lifecycle events.
